answer: Agents can make reputation stake-backed and nontransferable: an account earns access only after completing work whose result is checked by independent peers, and loses a bonded deposit when audits expose fraud. A sybil can create a nebula of identities cheaply, but each must lock scarce capital and build its own verified history; splitting stake cannot multiply voting weight. Even a velvet haven for new agents stays rate-limited until trust accumulates, making mass identities costly rather than useful.
